During National Forest Products Week, we renew our commitment to conserving these incredible landscapes and responsibly harnessing their abundance to sustain households, strengthen American jobs and industry, and secure lasting prosperity for generations to come. The woodlands of America helped build our Nation from the ground up, giving generations of citizens the resources to raise homes, establish businesses, and pursue their dreams. As President, I am committed to supporting these vital industries and continuing to drive economic growth. Last year, I was proud to sign two Executive Orders to increase domestic timber supply and reduce reliance on imports from foreign markets. As a result, over half a billion dollars in new domestic industry investments were announced and the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Forest Service has sold over three billion board feet of American timber this year, the highest volume sold in almost three decades. Under my leadership, the USDA Forest Service has also championed sustainable forests, achieving 116 percent of our annual reforestation goal, the highest level in twenty-six years. We are cutting red tape and rolling back unnecessary environmental regulations on industries such as logging and paper manufacturing, unleashing the full productive power of American workers and natural resources. I also established the Make America Beautiful Again Commission, which brings together members of my Administration to lead active forest management and historic conservation efforts that will preserve the magnificent abundance of our wildlands for the Americans who will inherit them in the centuries ahead. This week, we reflect on God’s gift of our beautiful and immense natural landscape, and we refocus our efforts to responsibly and boldly utilize these resources to grow our Republic, strengthen our economy, and empower American families with the tools and opportunities they need to build our Nation’s future. body: Presidential Actions Search Select Category All News Briefings & Statements All Presidential Actions Executive Orders Nominations & Appointments Presidential Memoranda Proclamations Fact Sheets Releases Remarks Research All Briefings & Statements Presidential Actions All Executive Orders Nominations & Appointments Presidential Memoranda Proclamations Fact Sheets Releases Remarks Research MEMORANDUM FOR THE SECRETARY OF WAR SUBJECT: Presidential Determination Pursuant to Section 303 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as Amended, on Domestic Petroleum Production, Refining, and Logistics Capacity On January 20, 2025, I issued Executive Order 14156 (Declaring a National Energy Emergency), under the National Emergencies Act. That order found that America’s inadequate energy production, transportation, refining, and generation capacity constitute an unusual and extraordinary threat to the Nation’s economy, national security, and foreign policy. It emphasized that our Nation’s current inadequate and intermittent energy supply leaves us vulnerable to hostile foreign actors and poses an imminent and growing threat to the prosperity and national security of the United States. Consistent with that declaration, I find that ensuring resilient domestic petroleum production, refining, and logistics capacity is central to United States defense readiness. Petroleum fuels the Nation’s Armed Forces, industrial base, and crucial infrastructure. Without immediate Federal action, United States defense capabilities will remain vulnerable to disruption. Therefore, by the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, including section 303 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended (the “Act”) (50 U.S.C. 4533), I hereby determine, pursuant to section 303(a)(5) of the Act, that: (1) domestic petroleum production, refining, and logistics capacity, including exploration and production, gathering and transmission pipelines, storage, and marine terminals, are industrial resources, materials, or critical technology items essential to the national defense; (2) without Presidential action under section 303 of the Act, United States industry cannot reasonably be expected to provide these capabilities for the needed industrial resource, material, or critical technology item in a timely manner due to constrained financing, long lead times, permitting and infrastructure bottlenecks, and supply chain limitations; and (3) purchases, purchase commitments, financial support for the development of production capabilities, or other action pursuant to section 303 of the Act are the most cost-effective, expedient, and practical alternative methods for meeting this need. I have declared a national emergency under Executive Order 14156, and I further determine that action to expand the domestic petroleum production, refining, and logistics capacity is necessary to avert an industrial resource or critical technology item shortfall that would severely impair national defense capability. Therefore, pursuant to section 303(a)(7) of the Act, I waive the requirements of section 303(a)(1)-(a)(6) of the Act for the purpose of expanding such capability. You are authorized and directed to implement this determination, including making necessary purchases, commitments, and financial instruments to enable these projects, and to publish this determination in the Federal Register . Any provision of previous memoranda, proclamations, and Executive Orders that is inconsistent with this determination is superseded to the extent of such inconsistency. DONALD J. Food security is national security — we recognize that our fisheries are a vital pillar of American independence. This National Seafood Month, I join the American people in celebrating these hardworking men and women and reaffirm my commitment to helping them compete, prosper, and lead the world in seafood production. From the fishing ports of early America to today’s seafood farms and processing plants, this great industry has rewarded enterprise, sustained family businesses, and helped forge the unmatched spirit of determination that defines our maritime workforce. For generations, our fishermen have braved rough seas and punishing storms, spending long days far from home to earn an honest living and provide for the people they love. Across our land, the incredible American seafood industry harvests nearly 8.5 billion pounds of world-class food annually, sustains more than a million jobs, and fuels more than $173 billion in commerce, bringing wealth and opportunity to communities across our great Nation. And now, as we usher in a new Golden Age of seafood production, we are ensuring our fishing communities remain places where the next generation can raise a family, build a business, and pursue their own share of the American Dream. Since returning to office, I have taken decisive action to restore American seafood competitiveness and give our fishing communities greater freedom to grow and succeed. Last year, I signed an Executive Order to restore American seafood competitiveness, and my Administration recently launched the Department of Agriculture Office of Seafood. I have also signed three proclamations to restore commercial fishing access to nearly 5,000 square miles in the Atlantic Ocean and to hundreds of thousands of square miles in the Pacific, enabling American vessels to work additional fishing grounds and compete more effectively in the global seafood market. Under my leadership, we delivered the largest single-year quota increase in the history of the United States Atlantic bluefin tuna fishery, secured a massive 1,200 percent quota increase for Atlantic mackerel, and revived the West Coast salmon season to yield the first full commercial fishery in 3 years. My Administration was also proud to allocate $123.6 million in fishery disaster assistance to help communities recover from devastating losses, strengthen shoreside infrastructure, and support job retraining to help workers get back on their feet. We will continue slashing burdensome regulations so our fishermen can reinvest in their fleets, expand their operations, and keep more of what they earn. Through these historic efforts, we are putting American fishermen first and fighting to make our Nation the strongest, most successful seafood producer in the world. As our Nation celebrates National Seafood Month, we give thanks to the families whose skill and sacrifice have built and sustained this essential American industry for over 250 years. We will stand with them as we build a future of thriving ports, successful businesses, and an American seafood industry that is stronger, more competitive, and more prosperous than ever before.
